Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks and the spreadsheet. We can accommodate the invoicing structure you outlined. High level options from our side (short form):

Option A — Single upfront invoice
- Redwood issues one invoice for $3,600,000 at contract signing.
- We provide an accounting memo and amortization schedule; revenue is deferred on our books and recognized monthly over the service period.
- Pro: Simplest cash flow for Redwood. Con: Cynosure's ledger shows single receipt unless you ask us to issue internal ledger splits (see B).

Option B — Split invoices issued at contract start
- Redwood issues three invoices today with separate invoice numbers and amounts for FY26/FY27/FY28 as you requested (we will date them at the start of each fiscal year if that helps).
- We still recognize revenue over service periods; the split only affects your AP/legal documentation and how you record cash received.
- Pro: Matches Cynosure budgeting. Con: Requires internal bookkeeping to allocate cash; still treated as prepaid on Redwood's balance sheet until recognized.

Option C — Staggered billing (invoices issued when each period begins)
- Redwood issues invoice 1 now, invoice 2 on 2027-10-01, invoice 3 on 2028-10-01.
- This is effectively a staged prepay which reduces upfront cash collection but is simplest for revenue mapping.

On the 15% discount: our commercial discount is tied to the committed term and to either (A) a single upfront payment or (B) a signed prepay agreement that covers the full term and amounts. If you choose Option C (staggered invoices and staggered payments), we'd need a contractual clause guaranteeing the committed term and amounts to preserve the discount (we can include a non-cancellation clause or a charge for early termination).

I copied Marissa and Karthik from Finance to confirm our revenue recognition wording and to propose invoice dates/amounts. Attached: Cynosure_SOW_v3.pdf and a zip of pro forma invoices for your review.

Next steps: Marissa — can you confirm that issuing three invoices today (dated 2026-10-01 / 2027-10-01 / 2028-10-01) is acceptable from Redwood's rev-rec perspective, and whether we should mark the later invoices as "advance invoices"?

Sarah — if you can confirm which option you prefer (A/B/C) and whether you require invoice dates to align exactly with your FY start, we'll draft the SOW/DocuSign.

Folks — confirming Finance position and recommended language for the memo Sarah needs. Short answers first:

- Can we issue three invoices dated 2026-10-01 / 2027-10-01 / 2028-10-01 at signing? Yes. We'll treat the invoices as advance invoices for cash receipt purposes.
- Does splitting change how Redwood recognizes revenue? No. Under ASC 606 we will defer revenue and recognize it ratably over the service period to which the invoices relate (monthly recognition across the 36 months). The invoices don't change recognition criteria; they change cash presentation for the customer.
- Discount: we will confirm in writing that the 15% term discount applies to the total $3,600,000 provided Cynosure signs the prepay agreement and the SOW (non-cancelable for the committed term). The discount is commercial and conditional on the full-term commitment, not on a single bank transfer.

Suggested memo language (one paragraph for auditors):
"Redwood Inference has received prepayment invoices totaling $3,600,000 for services to be delivered over a 36-month period beginning 2026-10-01. Redwood will record cash receipts as deferred revenue on its balance sheet upon receipt of payment and will recognize revenue in accordance with ASC 606/IFRS 15 on a monthly, straight-line basis over the covered service period. The issuance of multiple invoices at contract inception reflects allocation for customer budgeting and does not alter the period of performance or revenue recognition policy."

Accounting entries (high level):
- Upon receipt of payment(s): Debit Cash, Credit Deferred Revenue (liability) for corresponding amounts.
- Monthly recognition: Debit Deferred Revenue, Credit Revenue (monthly amortization).
